products.what_it_changes: Seller copy: ROCS opposing split clamps to improve stability and the fork's bending line, round clamping area under load, resists fork-leg rotation, independent preload per pinch bolt.

feedback.product: ROCS Tech triple clamps (standard offset, pressed stem) + PHDS bar mounts
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Standard-offset ROCS Tech (not adjustable Pro); bars in second hole closest to rider with PHDS mounts set back (closest to stock); stock medium PHDS elastomers; Renthal 839 Fatbar.
feedback.observed: Less vibration than OEM rubber-mounted bar mounts, especially at high rpm; better front tire contact on corner entry and more positive front feel in flat corners; less front-end wallow and more stable in deep ruts where stock clamps flexed; straight-line stability same as stock; slightly firmer on braking bumps and square edges. Can run lower pinch torque without fork slip. Fender and hour-meter mounts work. Cons: a couple hundred dollars more than other clamps; PHDS heavier than stock and fiddly to assemble; not compared against other aftermarket clamps.
feedback.measured: Price: clamps about $800; PHDS almost $200. OEM clamp torque 25 N-m bottom / 30 N-m top (X-Trig torque value not given).

feedback.product: FCP race cups, FCP head stays, titanium swingarm pivot axle and engine-mount bolts; stock-valved KYB baseline
feedback.publication: Vital MX forum (Moto-Related): 'Some Chassis and suspension work on the Triumph TF450'
feedback.author: lowmass
feedback.conditions: 180 lb expert vet; sand, loam and hard pack at three New York tracks; stock valving.
feedback.observed: Race cups: less high-speed chatter, more predictable steering, better corner traction, but front rode high so forks raised 2 mm in clamps and compression backed out 2 clicks. Head stays: square edges more rounded, less vibration above idle, slightly more at idle. Ti pivot and mount bolts: no clear difference. Overall more confidence and less effort; front still not as planted as a Honda. Follow-up (2026-05-20): polishing gear dogs/pockets, grinding a raised mark on the 3-4 shift fork and DLC-coating shift fork shafts (about $150) fixed shifting, no false neutrals in about 15 h. Reports about 3-week Triumph parts waits.
feedback.measured: Fork: 2 mm up in clamps, compression 15 out (stock 13), rebound 10 out, 0.48 kg/mm springs (stock 0.51), 350 cc 0W-16 motor oil per outer tube (stock 310 cc). Shock: 105 mm race sag, low-speed compression 16 out, rebound 12 out, high-speed compression 1 turn out. Rider notes the axle sat about 5 mm rearward of centre.
feedback.other_mods: FCP race cups, head stays, Ti pivot axle, two Ti engine-mount bolts; gearbox polishing and DLC shift-fork shafts

feedback.product: 2026 TF 250-X update: new airbox and silencer, revised mapping, Exedy clutch, retuned suspension
feedback.author: Triumph (ADB Magazine staff)
feedback.observed: New airbox and silencer for FIM/AMA sound rules; revised ECU mapping for power delivery and throttle response; new Exedy clutch (more torque capacity and durability); retuned suspension for mid-stroke control and cornering stability (no values); redesigned battery tray and oil sight glass; in-mould decals.

feedback.publication: Dirt Rider; Cycle News; Enduro21; Dirt Bike Magazine
feedback.author: Andrew Oldar (Dirt Rider); Cycle News Staff; Mark Tilley (Dirt Bike)
feedback.observed: Mapping, airbox/silencer and KYB settings carry over from the RC Edition. New: Exedy clutch hub, Belleville clutch spring, gearbox selector star, engine mounts, graphics. Standard launch control, traction control, quickshifter (2nd-5th), dual maps; optional MX Tune Pro app with accessory engine management unit unlocks up to ten more maps. D.I.D 520 SDH chain, JT lightweight sprockets, Neken clamps, ProTaper ACF bars, Galfer discs, Pirelli MX32.
feedback.measured: Claimed 61.5 hp at 9,500 rpm; 108.3 kg (Dirt Bike). Enduro21 lists 13/49 final drive and GBP 9,995. US price TBA at launch.

feedback.author: Robert Jones; Gray Van Dyke
feedback.conditions: Launch information after Triumph's MX2 title; no riding.
feedback.observed: Engine recalibrated for throttle response and torque delivery (claimed 47.4 hp unchanged); new valve guides; revised clutch (new clutch bearing and pack, Exedy Belleville spring); updated shift hardware; revised KYB settings with new toolless adjusters; updated Neken triple clamps; revised chain guide; new switchgear; all-black bodywork, redesigned fork guards. Carried over: Brembo, ProTaper ACF bars, Athena ECU, launch/traction control, quickshifter.

common_first_mods: Chassis feel before re-valve: X-Trig ROCS clamps (Keefer, TF 450-RC) and FCP race cups / head stays (Vital MX TF450 owner) both reported calmer front end and less vibration; the owner still wanted a re-valve.
Softer fork springs (0.48 vs stock 0.51 kg/mm) and 105 mm sag with shock high-speed compression 1 turn out for a 180 lb rider on a TF450 (one forum owner, stock valving).

Gearbox and clutch reliability work on TF 450: polished dogs and DLC shift-fork shafts (forum owner); Triumph itself added a new Exedy hub, Belleville spring and selector star for 2026 TF 450-X and a new clutch bearing/pack and shift hardware for 2027 TF 250-X.
gaps: Search budget for this session (200 searches shared by all agents) ran out after about 25 searches, so most priority brands were not reached. This file has 13 products and 5 findings, short of the 40-80 target.

Exhausts: no Akrapovic aftermarket (non-Triumph) TF part numbers, no SC-Project or Arrow TF listing found; DEP header has no part number or price. Whether 2024-2025 exhausts fit the 2026+ TF 250-X with its new airbox and silencer is not stated by any source.

ECU: GET SX1 PRO has no Triumph-specific part number; maker guide lists TF 250-X 2025, TF 450-RC 2025, TF 250-E / TF 450-E 2026 only; 2026-2027 X/C models not listed. Vortex and Twisted Development: nothing found.

Suspension: K-Tech Pro Valve fork/shock kits, springs, seal head and KYB sapphire stanchion for the TF 450-RC lack part numbers (product pages needed approval). No Factory Connection, Race Tech, Enzo, Pro Circuit or Dialed TF service listing found in the searches run.
Clamps/bar mounts: Luxon and Ride Engineering TF products not found; X-Trig ROCS Kit M12 (XT-40601005) may overlap the existing ROCS Tech record.
Brakes: Galfer is the OEM disc supplier (260/220 mm Disc Wave); no aftermarket Galfer, Braking or Moto-Master (beyond the existing supermoto kit) TF part numbers found.
Sprockets/chains and wheels: Supersprox, Renthal, JT, Haan, Kite, Warp 9 TF listings not found beyond what specialty files already hold.

Feedback: no 2026 TF 450-X or 2027 TF 250-X riding tests found; MXA, Racer X, Swapmoto, Vital MX test pages not reached. Retailers list a '2026-2027 TF 450-RC' (Scar, K-Tech) that no other source shows as a model year.
Vital MX TF450 owner thread does not give model year; FCP race cups fitment for Triumph unconfirmed.
